rekey_credit_registry.credit_ownership: Initial capacity B*R; ready projections use the unchanged original base and causal ACK anchor. The unique INIT gate deducts R once; ACK retains post_charge unchanged and starts the next idle anchor. Pending round time, peeks, REQUEST, cancellation and waiter changes never refill or reset the base.
rekey_credit_registry.qualification: Pure arithmetic only; no live owner, authenticated Artifact/TimeProfile, original causal clock anchor/incarnation, INIT ticket/deduction, ACK transition, pending-round exclusion, service/work/crypto/cleanup reservation, timer or provider/production qualification. Default zero additional authorized time tolerance; no implicit skew.

crypto_usage_registry.counting: Seal and open are accounted separately at key, epoch and Session levels; open includes failed attempts. Ciphertext includes the tag; authentication blocks include actual AAD, payload and one length block.
crypto_usage_registry.reservation: Precharge at the original atomic send ticket or receive crypto-dispatch gate; cancelled or unused precharges never refund cryptographic usage. Memory/work reference exit is separate. Rekey preserves Session totals; a new scope preserves epoch totals. Time is revalidated at actual crypto start.
crypto_usage_registry.qualification: Fixed operational limits and pure arithmetic only; no independent aggregate cryptographic proof, owner/atomic reservation, soft watermarks, maintenance reserve, actual provider/AEAD invocation, root age enforcement, key cleanup or production qualification

time_arithmetic_registry.qualification: Exact conservative integer arithmetic only; no clock or source authentication, nonce matching, profile qualification, incarnation continuity, anchor installation, owner/timer state, gate reopening, resource reservations or production SDK/provider qualification

resource_formula_registry.qualification: Body buffers, permanent bitmap and enumerated application baseline only; no full ready_min, short-work floor, actual object charge, reservation or physical-memory qualification

ready_vector_plan.source: RFC8032 section 7.1 public signer seeds and captured Noise roots; synthetic context digests, not authenticated credentials

error_registry_boundary.allocation: Numeric codes are candidates under design 6.1/6.2, scoped to their named registry; no runtime dispatch is qualified.
error_registry_boundary.retry: preserve_facts grants no replay, same-lease retry, automatic reconnect or execution authority. Subsequent actions require original owner and layered commit facts under 5.1/6.1. retryable only permits an optional retry_after_ms hint.
error_registry_boundary.admission: FSA4 status=1 rejects this handshake, not the durable admission record. Store failure, unknown commit or unproven epoch never clears admitted/spent/unknown facts or restarts the original guard. These bytes require a valid original response/signing owner.
error_registry_boundary.locality: Session ERROR codes apply only after the 3.5.2 attribution gate rules out local isolation. Stream ERROR codes require an existing trusted owner. Application/RPC/TopUp/local-only results never use this L0 registry.
error_registry_boundary.close: ERROR action applies to ERROR only. CLOSE uses its target; GOAWAY seals admission while retaining existing streams. None of these frames replaces terminal proof. Normal code 0 carries no success or commit evidence.

byte_allocations.profile_revision: 4; shared by Artifact.contract_revision, hello, TransportContext and the single LP(profile/revision) prologue term
byte_allocations.dh_algorithm: NoiseStaticPublicKey: x25519=0, p256=1; exactly one key and matching complete crypto profile
byte_allocations.features: datagram bit0, application progress resume bit1; mandatory identity/content protection has no feature bit
byte_allocations.artifact_contract: Artifact uses design field IDs 0..27 and artifact_version text 4. SessionContract IDs 0..6 are max_frame, max_streams, max_credit, idle_duration_ms, rekey_envelope, application_profile and conditional rpc_max_general_outstanding; application_profile is transport=0, services=1, execution=2. ResumePolicy IDs 0..4 are enabled, purpose, scope, max_issued_token_duration_ms and max_token_bytes; purpose/scope have the sole value 0. SpendPolicy field 0 is mode=0 mandatory_once.
byte_allocations.leg_route: Leg IDs 0..13 are a shared closed access-class union; carrier raw_quic=0, websocket=1, webtransport=2. Route IDs 0..4 contain path_kind, candidate_id and applicable complete legs. Candidate retains design IDs 0..6. Its route projection is generated from the named registry membership without priority or dependency refs.
byte_allocations.origin_schemes: Reference RFC6454/WHATWG tuple schemes http, https, ws, wss and ftp with their fixed default ports. Unknown schemes fail as unregistered; this draft does not impose an http/https-only product policy or qualify custom scheme semantics.
byte_allocations.pool_selection: Field 7 of the existing 17-field proof is bytes16 for live and PoolSelectionRef for pool; immutable source context selects the variant. PoolSelectionSet derives exact index/candidate/complete-route references from the complete signed Artifact. Distinct candidate-set and route-set domains bind the same complete map without embedding it in the proof.
byte_allocations.pool_indices: Zero-based Artifact.candidates indices, strictly increasing and unique; actual member, digest and ParentWinner checks remain mandatory
byte_allocations.pool_authority: OnceAuthorityRef binds tenant, parent issuer and the stable logical spend/winner authorities without conveying a store location or caller-selected authority
byte_allocations.qualification: These are candidate registry allocations under design 6.2, not an architecture change or evidence of runtime or cryptographic qualification.

deferred_constraints: Registry allocation under 3.9.1/4.1.1/6.2: one immutable connection_activation authorization for one parent issuer and logical SpendLedger authority in the parent namespace/generation. Purpose 1 is connection_activation, not revocation_head. Independent TrustConfig authenticates the whole entry; it has no self-signature or renewal path. signing_key_id fixes original public key, purpose and all bounds; changed authorization requires a new ID. The inclusive parent cohort range and absolute admission/Session bounds intersect the original parent, fixed capacity H_connection and original cohort policy. The signer issuer_key_id is its immutable bytes16 revocation identity, distinct from the allowed parent artifact_issuer_key_id; it is part of the same independently authenticated entry. Its explicit original connection impact is last_parent_cohort and certificate impact is null. Complete independent trust, parent authority continuity, all original permission history, revocation and durable retirement remain external gates.

Caller identity is the stable authenticated application execution principal, not a Session or certificate identifier. Independent application recovery keys, current caller/tenant/audience/service authorization, trusted time, policy TTL/count/store quotas and original operation history are separate gates. Field IDs and finite byte limits are registry allocations under 3.7.3/6.2.

The SDK captures the exact new ready Session transport context, accepted application Stream and local incarnation before preparing/saving. Original operation/digest, checkpoint and generation must match the protected token. Only an authenticated application transaction can consume the token, advance generation and bind the target. No new L0 frame or Session-secret recovery.

Accepted requires confirmed progress. Rejected/unknown may report already confirmed application progress or omit it; no transport ACK inference. Current authorization, original response ownership, result limits and transaction evidence remain external.

These codes describe ordinary RPC message stopping and bounded service refusals/errors; service errors require the original complete-input gate. Original channel/direction/reply serial and response-owner gates remain required. request_message_aborted confirms only incomplete input for this serial, without validating its declared execution digest or asserting global nonexecution. response_output_stopped ends output only. No raw cause, execution assertion, retry or dispatch authority is carried.

All original issuer/delegation authorization evidence for this revoked key, sorted by unique authorization_digest. This entry does not authenticate membership, permit trust retirement or install GC authority.
Complete original certificate digest/cohort/expiry evidence only. Namespace/generation, authenticated State membership, original certificate identity and safe retirement remain external.

Original parent Artifact evidence only. The containing authenticated State supplies namespace/generation. Full Session/activation/grant impact, permanent frontier installation, once retention and real reference exit remain external.

Complete original permission history, same issuer/namespace attribution and permanent trust retirement are not established by this map.

Independent TrustConfig must authenticate the exact immutable namespace mapping. Structural validation and numeric compatibility do not prove publication provenance, real service capacity or original authorization.

Independent TrustConfig must authenticate this exact immutable reference. Its requirements apply through the complete original role-specific credential closure; policy names and revisions do not order security strength.

Independent TrustConfig must authenticate this immutable namespace mapping. Structural validation neither authorizes subscription nor proves full State/index/workspace/cleanup capacity or deployment workload qualification.

This entry is authenticated by the independent TrustConfig; it is not self-signed. Registry purpose 0 means revocation_head. Original independent authorization, fixed publication policy, capacity and trusted time remain mandatory.

Verify independent root/delegation/signature, exact immutable capacity/publication/generation binding and trusted interval before accepting Head facts. Complete State matching, publication snapshot/time provenance and atomic observed/pinned/active continuity remain separate gates.

This shared grammar requires exact application-header variant presence and constants. Business and SDK errors bind the original request. Dedicated stream errors terminate output; Resume has exact request/response variants. No current contract, authentication, ownership or dispatch authority is established.
Known digest requires the original complete immutable verified contract body held throughout the query. These field IDs are registry allocations under design 3.7.3.
Current caller authorization, exact trusted source and the fixed query owner/resource vector remain runtime requirements.

Applicable Offer presence and all membership checks require the original target and complete exact contract. Status bytes are not evidence of current permission or registration.

The opaque application definition must match its exact trusted local schema/codec and real content selection/read/retention contract before registration or Bind. Structural bytes do not install code or attest storage.

Exact trusted MethodDefinition identity, caller authorization and real registered semantics must match before installation or execution. Byte validation grants no authority, capacity, deduplication, durable retention, checkpoint support or publication qualification.

The draft registry allocates revision identifiers as canonical security_id text and positive uint32 message caps; this does not constrain raw Stream payloads.

Nonempty ordinary metadata only; zero bytes is the sole empty sentinel at the containing bytes API. Namespace/version registration, immutable projections, authentication and pending-to-rejected ownership remain runtime qualifications.

Full original OPEN bytes bind each application value. No live admission, I/O ownership, callback, allocator or cleanup qualification is claimed.

application_sdk_errors.boundary: Ordinary RPC stops and bounded service errors use the original ReplySlot and response association. Dedicated streaming SDK errors use the original single-item/error reservation, terminate output and are followed by CloseWrite; RPC ABORT/STOP codes are forbidden on streams. Complete-input, current authorization, exact service admission and publication gates remain mandatory. No code asserts global nonexecution, retry permission or delivery. Management and Resume errors remain separate. source_overflow is exclusive to dedicated streaming; it seals the original SDK event source without asserting nonexecution.

application_headers.boundary: Exact request, success/item, fixed read/management, business-error and SDK-error headers. Business errors obey original payload limits; the registered SDK error variants use the fixed small-error reservation. Streaming errors terminate the original dedicated stream without a new transport frame. Authentication, current routing, actual owners/resources, application codecs and dispatch remain external gates. Resume uses its own bounded request/result payloads on an already accepted target Stream; token trust, ownership and transaction facts remain external.

connection_assurance_registry.boundary: Finite direct WebSocket capability definitions only. Provider and complete signed-route binding plus actual preparation are mandatory. TLS13 describes only the observing consumer leg; accepted observers cannot attest a remote consumer. This table neither qualifies implementations nor enables a deployment or runtime. Native/relay independent progress, isolation and datagram definitions require their complete original provider integration and qualification.

boundary.connection: ConnectionRequirements only tightens the original material and immutable application plan. A missing application_profile adopts the signed profile subject to local plan requirements. ConnectionGuarantees and SessionInfo are detached semantic projections, with no route, endpoint, provider or stable digest. Scope covers the complete path; local_consumer_tls13_verification covers only the observing consumer network leg. Within-profile assumptions include cooperating authenticated peers, admitted finite resources and scheduling, and exclude Session rekey freezes, shared maintenance failures and hard authorization/crypto deadlines. Schema validation is not evidence of provider or remote deployment capability; original Prepare, pre-spend and final publication gates must supply and recheck actual observations.
boundary.errors: Only the allocated protocol-error subset is projected. The code, scope and preserve_facts disposition are selected by a trusted owner after attribution; validation does not authorize retry, reconnect or replay. Local/application/connection error allocations remain incomplete.
boundary.read: ReadContext is private trusted original-owner validation input, not a public result or wire field. start_offset is the ordinary call start or fixed cursor start; transferred is the actual ordinary handoff count or current internal cursor filled. stream_status is the committed fact at this result gate. The reference does not perform I/O, claim handoff, acquire ownership, scan a retained canceled prefix, reserve memory or grant credit. Production owners must establish these facts and enforce all original gates.
boundary.read_method_failure: Method failures have no ReadResult payload or wait status. cursor is present exactly when the original cursor exists; transferred_bytes is cumulative Stream-to-cursor movement and remains accurate after delivery or abandonment. Private context binds the fixed start/target, original failure gate, committed stream/error/cause and lifecycle facts. It is captured by that owner, never inferred from caller-supplied metadata. Local time/authorization/resource failures do not manufacture a Stream error or replace an existing EOF/abort. Invalid arguments and target mismatches are checked before delivery state; TakePrefix may freeze an existing waiter. Native error wrappers retain finite SDK reason identities, not provider chains.
boundary.cleanup: pending means unfinished obligations, not proof that Close was requested. Only actual core resource exit plus zero owned pending callbacks permits complete; independently transferred result owners are excluded. Incomplete wait observations do not change lifecycle or permanently overwrite owner progress. This detail snapshot is not the complete object_kind/lifecycle_state/reason envelope, which remains unresolved; no combination commands parent closure or reconnect.
boundary.close: send_drained and read_terminal are independent authenticated direction facts. Cleanup or callback success cannot synthesize them. First-error preservation, normal_auto_destroy and adapter behavior require runtime qualification.
boundary.write: WriteProgress counts the original request's local application acceptance, not tickets, acknowledgements or delivery. Prepared has no accepted bytes; running has no terminal reason; terminal completion is stable. Internal reference allocation of phase/reason names grants no Start/retry or runtime owner authority. Complete acceptance may coexist with pending cleanup.
boundary.transfer: TransferContext is a private trusted original-owner fact, not public or wire input. The difference between source reads and destination acceptance is at most one finite chunk and is preserved exactly in the result tail or by an explicit source adapter. Source-retained counts do not prove ownership or data integrity; real atomic handoff, bounded backing, lifecycle and adapter qualification remain required.
boundary.duplex: DuplexResult projects the original bridge's two directions without endpoint objects or identities. The target endpoint kind is fixed by the original owner: only flowersec_stream reports authenticated send_drained, while native_duplex reports only its actual native_send_finished half-close/completion guarantee. Private nested contexts bind counts, source status, target completion and terminal outcome; self-reported input is not evidence. At least one endpoint must be Flowersec. Normal transfer requires both source EOFs, complete target sends and no unaccepted tail/first error, independently of pending/incomplete cleanup; overall success additionally requires cleanup complete. The current TypedError subset does not allocate all native/local first causes. Runtime distinct-endpoint/alias and full-owner checks, actual half-close capability, first-cause preservation, final progress sealing, tail handoff, charge/cleanup, cancellation/drop and real bridge execution remain unqualified.
boundary.publication: ResponsePublicationStatus is the finite original handler-response observation. Only original response selection plus complete final-byte provider handoff before an earlier terminal failure permits flushed; internal acceptance, ReplySlot release, replacement/error/ABORT publication, peer receipt and maintenance success are different facts. Unknown requires one exact finite original cause; other states carry no cause. Later provider tails cannot regress flushed or reopen an unknown outcome. Non-restart methods report only not_applicable. Private context describes the original publisher's already ordered facts, not untrusted evidence. PublicationTransferResult names the existing TransferTo outcomes without implementing transfer or granting publication/restart/replay authority. Original request/channel association, callback/selection gates, actual provider offsets, deadlines, transfer/observer lifetime and cleanup require runtime qualification.
